items.title: Reconvene to Open Session / Roll Call
Report Out on Closed Session from April 1, 2026

publicComments.name: Aida Vázquez
publicComments.summary: Spoke in Spanish (with board translation) as a Garfield School parent to oppose proposed changes to bilingual programs, arguing that the current bilingual program has been effective for her children and many families and should be strengthened rather than changed.

publicComments.name: Michelle Strode
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of incoming TK parents at Orion's Mandarin Immersion Program, requested expansion of after-school programs (Play Thrive) to accommodate working families whose TK placement is not viable without reliable after-school care.

publicComments.name: Sally Dunaway Young
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for expanding the Mandarin Immersion TK program but urged allocation of additional campus space so that aftercare providers can expand to serve working families whose children cannot participate without afternoon coverage.

publicComments.name: May Liang
publicComments.summary: Advocated for the expansion of Play Thrive after-school program at Orion, sharing that her daughter secured a kindergarten spot but the family was waitlisted for after-school care, and requested a third classroom be added.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: As a parent whose child attended Mandarin Immersion and now attends North Star Academy, thanked Superintendent Baker for his long-standing support of both programs.

publicComments.name: Josh Hill
publicComments.summary: Echoed other parents' excitement about the Orion Mandarin program acceptance for his child while expressing anxiety about after-school care availability and requesting program expansion.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez-Monet
publicComments.summary: As a longtime Hoover community volunteer and parent, advocated for smaller class sizes, noting that the single Spanish kindergarten class at Hoover has grown too large and students with varied needs are not receiving adequate individual attention.

publicComments.name: Sophia Santos
publicComments.summary: As a first grade teacher at Hoover with 27 students including high proportions of IEP, multilingual, and behavioral-needs students, urged the board to prioritize manageable class sizes citing research showing smaller class sizes improve academic and social outcomes.

publicComments.name: Kristy Herrera
publicComments.summary: As a Hoover kindergarten teacher with deep personal roots in RCSD as a former student, parent, and 34-year educator, passionately urged the board to invest in smaller class sizes and equitable distribution of students across the district, arguing the current system is neither equal nor equitable.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: As CSEA Redwood City Chapter 5 President, briefly introduced herself and Clifford representative Kristy Jackson and expressed eagerness to hear the school reports and the RCTA presentation.
